overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the emails about COVID-era meeting scheduling were procedural, and a councilor's reply on case reporting was not deliberation. Review was limited to the five emails named in the complaint.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council deliberated outside a posted meeting via four emails from March-April 2020 about meeting status and format during COVID-19.
allegations.key_passage: We find that all of these emails regarding when and how to meet were merely administrative in nature pertaining to the scheduling of meetings, fitting squarely within the exception of the definition of deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a councilor's reply-all email on COVID-19 case reporting, sent after a Mayor's Office report, was deliberation outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: On these facts, we do not find that Member Murphy’s emails constituted “deliberation” as defined by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant pointed to many more emails than the five named in the complaint; the AG limited review to the emails specified in the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Although Mr. DeLacey provided us with copies of many more emails during our investigation, we limit our review here to the emails Mr. DeLacey specified in his complaint.
